In article <3ictvr$4...@newsbf02.news.aol.com> curt...@aol.com (CurtAdams) writes:
>
>My proposal was to make the cost of WwEF (currently nothing) commensurate
>with the benefit (a free action). I agree restricting WwEF is a dud
>solution, for exactly the reason you mention.
>
>My personal take on restriction is that it is a very clunky solution. If
>I hand you a deck, it takes you up to 10 minutes to check for card limits,
>depending on the complexity of the card limits. It should never be so
>difficult to discover if someone is cheating. It is also very easy to
>accidentally go over a card limit without noticing, if more than a few
>card are subject to limits.

Heartly agreed. Card restrictions were used because cards are
unbalanced. Balancing the cards is the real, true solution.
With really balanced cards, you don't need card restrictions.

If you restrict everyone to 4 Wakes, I'll bet you that everyone
who have 4 Wakes will put them all in. Even if you /know/ that
your predator has 20 Change of Targets in his deck, you'll
still definitely put those 4 Wakes in. This is evidence
of an unbalanced card, the thing that made Magic into
a $$$ game.

Alan.

>Doesn't WwEF say "allows a vampire to block and play reaction cards as if
>untapped"?
>
>If you've got a card that allows you to mess with the bleed on the other side
>of the table, fine, if not, tough luck.
>

Well, it doesn't say you must _succeed_ in blocking, or reacting, it just
allows you to try. If you fail, you remain tapped and discard the card,
thus getting it out of your hand.

If you are unable to block an action, you fail.

Thus you can discard it on any action, blockable or not.

"My minion wakes up... and fails to block..."

-Jeff Bergan

In article <D4rp9...@undergrad.math.uwaterloo.ca> bwr...@calum.csclub.uwaterloo.ca (Kernel Mustard) writes:

>
>I'll agree that the distribution has a lot of powerful, very useful
>cards at common rarity. Most of the more powerful rarer cards seem
>to be balanced with (D) actions possible against them. Still,
>there are a good number of uncommon cards you should have to
>build a solid deck. Sports bikes are as desirable as wwef's in
>any deck I build or have seen (Mr. Winthrop is just a rare version,
>but equally valued). KRCG is pretty much the same. (You really
>can't survive without the perminent intercept, it might
>not stop S&B, but the difficulty goes up, besides messing with
>his equips, torpor visits, hunting, +1 steath directed action verses
>your Powerbase are invaluable). Hunting grounds are desirable in
>any deck with a fair number of vampires from any one clan (heh,
>free blood, suck that back up your blood doll and you're in combo
>heaven... do I want the blood... or does Anvil get it). Arcane Library,
>Eco Terrorist, and Art Museum pretty much automatically fit into
>decks build around the respective clans (at least these are rare,
>but they're still no-brainers).

Yes, those cards are quite useful. However, equipment and locations
usually cost pool - that's where the balance comes along.
Sports bikes cost 1 pool, and an action to get it, and it is
useable only by the minion who currently has it. If you
manage to torporize the vampire with the sports bike as
he blocks you,
that's one more lost pool; even if another of his vampires
takes it, it costs another action, and also another turn
where the SB cannot be used (barring a WwEF).

KRCG is good, but again it costs pool - this time 2 pool.
And there are many ways to mess with a location: Arson,
Disputed Territory, etc. If it succeeds, that's
2 pool down the drain. Also, if your predator has
more pool than you, he can simply contest it
and force you to yield, and that's again 2 pool
down the drain.

Hunting Grounds, again, cost 2 pool. The problem is with
the Blood Doll, not the Hunting Ground; without
convenient ways of moving blood from vampire to
pool (Blod Doll, Minion Tap), a Hunting Ground
is useful, but just that.

Sorry that I don't know too much about the rest of the
clan-specific locations you mentioned.

Maybe the problem of the game is the existence of
some gross combos that allow you to gain a lot
of pool; if pool becomes a very real concern,
and a very limited resource, players will think
a bit more before banging down those Sports Bikes
and locations. More sports bikes and locations
would mean less vampires.

Also, if your group has a 2-card limit, it might
make it virtually infeasible to build a combat
deck that does not rely heavily on weapons;
also, the 2-card limit makes it hard to use
discipline stealth/intercept. Without powerful
combat decks to keep intercept in check, and
while non-permanent stealth/intercept is
hindered, of course permanent intercept becomes
so much more important.

>There are several more, but we all know the familiar cards we see again
>and again (Heh, you're common list didn't meantion Army of Rats with goes
>in any animalism deck).

Gangrel and Nosferatsu don't have bleed modifiers.
They need Army of Rats to force their prey to
fight them. I may have a suggestion for Revised:
without superior Animalism, AoR cost 1 vampire blood.

>Also, wwef's a good card for
>the sake of the game. It allows people to do more actions on
>their turn that normal (even if they only bluff having one in the
>hand). This makes games move faster, everybody does more actions
>trying to get the opponent to misplay a wwef on something they
>son't care for (part of the stategy that's key to the game
>is not wasting them before your opponenent does).

This is a good point. However, making WwEF cost 1 blood
to play doesn't change its usefulness in this concept,
IMO.

As a side note, whenever someone mentions the strategy
of bluffing so that opponent blocks/Wakes your
unimportant actions, I'll think: "That's a useful
strategy, but why not build my deck so that
every action is important and deadly, so that
opponent is screwed no matter what." I understand
that this is somewhat hard to do with a 2-card
(or even a 4-card) limit. Just my $.02 .

>I don't see
>fireballs and disintegrates being restricted in magic (or modified),
>and they're much worse that wwef for the game.

Well, it's not hard to find people here in rec. .. .jyhad
who would agree with me that MtG is a much worse /game/
than Jyhad.

:-)

>The card that
>should be removed or updated is Misdirection. It causes people
>to not do actions, play conservatively, bring out hordes of minions,
>and then have the game drag for a really long period or time while
>the players wait to draw a Misdirection and be able to bleed out
>their prey (sounds a lot like fireballs, but this is worse...
>at least against a fireball player you can play all out in an
>attempt to kill him first).

I do agree that Misdirection is "too cheap" and should have its
cost raised by 1 or 2, but if the above situation happens
often in your games, there may be a problem in everyone's
deck. Possibly, because of the 2-card limit, no one
has a deck effective enough to do anything.
If someone has an effective combat/S&B/political/
innovative-but-effective deck, we shall see
constant action ...

>and then have the game drag for a really long period or time while
>the players wait to draw a Misdirection and be able to bleed out
>their prey (sounds a lot like fireballs, but this is worse...
>at least against a fireball player you can play all out in an
>attempt to kill him first).

This complaint occurs when people play with card limits. WwEF hoses
Misdirection nicely (and still would, even with a blood cost). If one can
only have 4, or 2 - Misdirect away!

A side comment - an EFFECTIVE card hoser is another card which (a) hurts
the user of the hosed card more than the hoser and (b) has uses even if
the other player doesn't have the target. If one of the two attributes is
REALLY good, you can do without the other.

Minion taps and asendence, I tend not to use much. You ain't gonna

I'll agree that the distribution has a lot of powerful, very useful
cards at common rarity. Most of the more powerful rarer cards seem
to be balanced with (D) actions possible against them. Still,
there are a good number of uncommon cards you should have to
build a solid deck. Sports bikes are as desirable as wwef's in
any deck I build or have seen (Mr. Winthrop is just a rare version,
but equally valued). KRCG is pretty much the same. (You really
can't survive without the perminent intercept, it might
not stop S&B, but the difficulty goes up, besides messing with
his equips, torpor visits, hunting, +1 steath directed action verses
your Powerbase are invaluable). Hunting grounds are desirable in
any deck with a fair number of vampires from any one clan (heh,
free blood, suck that back up your blood doll and you're in combo
heaven... do I want the blood... or does Anvil get it). Arcane Library,
Eco Terrorist, and Art Museum pretty much automatically fit into
decks build around the respective clans (at least these are rare,
but they're still no-brainers).

There are several more, but we all know the familiar cards we see again

and again (Heh, you're common list didn't meantion Army of Rats with goes

in any animalism deck). Anyways, my point is that, yes, wwef is the best
card in the game, but it's COMMON. That means it doesn't take a lot
of work to get them (moxen and lotus were somewhat easier to get
before they were discontinued but they still commanded at least
the value of a good rare card). Also, wwef's a good card for

the sake of the game. It allows people to do more actions on
their turn that normal (even if they only bluff having one in the
hand). This makes games move faster, everybody does more actions
trying to get the opponent to misplay a wwef on something they
son't care for (part of the stategy that's key to the game

is not wasting them before your opponenent does). I don't see

fireballs and disintegrates being restricted in magic (or modified),

and they're much worse that wwef for the game. The card that

should be removed or updated is Misdirection. It causes people
to not do actions, play conservatively, bring out hordes of minions,
and then have the game drag for a really long period or time while
the players wait to draw a Misdirection and be able to bleed out
their prey (sounds a lot like fireballs, but this is worse...
at least against a fireball player you can play all out in an
attempt to kill him first).

if there's a chance that the card can be used, it can be played. And

lot freer in Jyhad than Magic. As it should be.

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
>Okay, let me get this straight. The reason you think that WwEF are so
>powerfull is that you can burn them whenever you feel like it?

No, the reason it's so powerful is that with a good Wake collection every
vampire can act every turn and still block. Waky-waky Tremere or Toreador
decks are a fearsome sight. The burn business is a side issue. Someone
said that sometimes you won't want to wake (i.e., Gangrel bleeds, etc.)
and the Wakes will jam up your hand. I and others pointed out in those
occasional situations, you can just ditch the Wakes to get other cards in
your hand.

>We play with a four card limit of everything (mostly cuz of
>Malk decks) and i haven't seen anything get out of hand with these cards.

>I think it's another case of people whining about cards they can't deal
>with.

4 card limits to stop Malk decks is an excellent case of cutting off your
nose to spite your face. Malk decks work fine with 4-card limits because
there are 4 different Obfuscate stealth cards, 4 different Dominate bleed
boosters, etc. Several anti-Malk decks,on the other hand, get shut down
by 4-card limits; rush combat will toast Malks nicely, but not with only 4
Bum's Rushes.

At the same time, you make Misdirection unbelieveably powerful (not enough
untaps), make Brujah unable to resist Protean aggravated damage (twice as
many aggro damage as Sideslips), and shut down a variety of decks -
Fortitude combat (which needs Traps) anti-intercept weenies (not enough
Zip Guns/ Dragonbreath rounds), etc.

The viability of a deck should not depend on the number of cards of a
given type included in the set. It creates very bizarre effects.

I want Wakes fixed because I've seen several people quit because they
couldn't get enough Wakes to play. Not everyone wants to buy a whole box
to get 4. I also think it's sloppy design to make a card much better than
others. Cards should be of roughly equal power - THAT will make for
maximum variety in decks, not stereotyped groupings of 4 cards each (like
magic).

Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

Messages.Author: CurtAdams

>> "My minion wakes up... and fails to block..."

>Peace Jeff,
>Only actions of your predator, prey, or directed actions (targetted at
>you) from another meth. If you had Anneka in play, yes, you could play
>WwEF on _any_ action.

I'm starting to feel like a broken record here, but-

WwEF says "usable by a tapped vampire"

It does NOT say "Usable by a tapped vampire which may make a legal attempt
to block".

It does NOT say "Usable by a tapped vampire if you have a usable reaction
card to play in your hand"

Note the difference with 2nd Tradition - "Usable by tapped vampire which
untaps and attempts to block". That IS restricted to a vampire which may
attempt to block.

The only restrictions on the use of WwEF are that it is a reaction card,
and may not be played on your turn, and that the using vampire must be
tapped. Note that since it doesn't actually untap the vampire, one vampire

could pitch multiple Wakes at once - he is still tapped and eligible to
play a second after the first

Different kinds of actions have restrictions on who can block, but
reaction cards, in general, are a legal response to any action,by any
player.

Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

Oops. You forgot something. A vampire can't play the same
reaction card twice during the same action. Don't get carried away in
the example.
Now, one *player* could pitch multiple WwEF's at once, providing
that he had multiple tapped vampires, but once *vampire* is stuck to
once per action.

>No, the reason it's so powerful is that with a good Wake collection every

>occasional situations, you can just ditch the Wakes to get other cards in
>your hand.

Well, I have two comments here. First, I will preface it by
saying that I agree that WwEF is a powerful card, so don't think I'm
arguing that point. Again, I'm *not* arguing that WwEF is a powerful
card.
However, WwEF's *will* jam up your hand during combat in any
deck that cycles if you have (the number you gave me) 10 to 12 of them.
Any combat deck that cycles has the problem of an occasional jam. If
you're using the tactics you gave me earlier (equipment and retainers
for permanent bonuses instead of combat cards), you're increasing the
odds of a combat jam, and in a combat deck, *that's* exactly when you
don't want to jam up. There's no way to ditch extra WwEF's in combat,
nor any other card that's not a combat card. I'm not afraid of a
Tremere who can't get a strike card because he's busy cycling through
WwEF's. Or Master cards. Or Bleeds. Whatever. *Any* card in that
amount will hold you up in combat.
Second, there are quite a few strategies out there where it
doesn't matter whether or not they can block you. I mean, WwEF or not,
there's practically *always* gonna be at least one vampire out who can
block you. The question is how you deal with that. If you haven't
built a deck that deals with that, you're playing the wrong game.
